content: In the field of chemistry, a basic oxide is defined as an oxide that can either: 1. React with water, resulting in the transfer of a proton to the oxide. 2. React with an acid to produce a salt. Examples of basic oxides include the following: Sodium oxide (Na₂O): This compound reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide (NaOH). Magnesium oxide (MgO): When magnesium oxide reacts with water, it forms magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)₂). Copper(II) oxide (CuO): This oxide reacts with nitric acid (HNO₃) to yield copper nitrate (Cu(NO₃)₂) and water (H₂O). The reaction can be represented as: CuO + 2HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + H₂O Basic oxides are typically oxides of metals.
